messages:
Claire: Heads-up — Enterprise customer 'acme-ml' is hitting a lot of 429s and complaining about slow tail latency since last night. Raised to us via support ticket. They say it started after a marketing burst. Can we triage? :eyes:

Devon: Seen the ticket. They include an example request that returns 429 and then long 5xx/timeout spikes. Customer says calls are to the /v1/generate -> model: redwood-13b-qat.

Ram: I pulled logs for that org id. There's a sudden spike at 03:12 UTC where concurrent ephemeral workers jumped from ~12 -> ~220 for that org. Token volume spiked too. I see throttling counters flip on the ingress side: `redwood.throttled.count{reason=\"quota_exhausted\",org=\"acme-ml\"}`.

SRE-Oncall-Bot: Alert fired: quota_exhaustion_alert (severity=warning) for org=acme-ml at 2026-11-21T03:14:08Z.

Devon: Good find. Two immediate questions: 1) Are these 429s coming from a per-customer quota (token or RPS) or global token buckets? 2) Which route/model label is getting most of the hits so we can attribute?

Ram: From the policy table, acme-ml is on a per-org RPS limit of 2000 req/min and per-token burst of 1M tokens/day. The spike breached the RPS first. The throttling metric has labels: `{route=/v1/generate,model=redwood-13b-qat,org=acme-ml}`. So attribution seems clear: route+model+org.

Claire: Can we reproduce locally (or in staging) to confirm? What exact request shape? Customer provided this minimal repro: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-qat","input":"summarize: \"long document repeated\"","max_tokens":1024}'` They said they were running a fan-out across 50 clients at once.

Devon: Steps to reproduce I used in a private sandbox: 50 threads making that curl every 300ms for 10 minutes -> RPS ~166. Because each request returns 1024 tokens the downstream token throughput becomes large. Key point: small concurrency but large tokens_per_req causes token throttles to trigger bucket exhaustion and backend queueing -> higher latency and 429s on ingress.

Ram: Dashboard checks to run (Grafana/Prometheus):
- Panel: `sum(rate(redwood.requests.total[1m])) by (org,route,model)` to see realtime RPS
- Panel: `increase(redwood.throttled.count[5m]) by (reason,org,route,model)` for attribution
- Panel: `redwood.tokens.sent_per_minute` by org -> to correlate token consumption jumps
- Heatmap: request latency p50/p95/p99 by org and model

Claire: Also check logs for `X-RateLimit-Reset` and response headers from the ingress. Devs: do we emit `X-RateLimit-*` for per-org quotas?

Devon: Yes — for per-org token/RPS quotas we send `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` on 200/429 responses. In this customer's logs I see many 429s without `Remaining` > 0.

Support-Bot: Customer provided timestamps and request IDs: [req-88c3, req-88c4, req-88d9]. Logged and attached to ticket.

Claire: Short-term mitigation options we can offer to customer: 1) Temporary quota bump (increase RPS for 24h) 2) Backoff/retry guidance with exponential jitter 3) Recommend model shard/variant or smaller `max_tokens` and using streaming to reduce token spikes.

Ram: Ops actions I've taken: added a temporary org override to raise RPS for acme-ml from 2000 -> 8000 for 6 hours. Also toggled more workers to their region to drain queued requests. Monitoring: I set an ad-hoc Grafana panel `acme-ml: throttle attribution` and added an alert for `increase(redwood.throttled.count{org=\"acme-ml\"}[2m]) > 50` to page SRE if it repeats.

Kai: For longer-term: we should surface per-route per-model throttling in the Console. Current gaps: the Console shows org-level quota usage but not a breakdown by model/route. Proposed metric to add: `redwood.throttled.by_route{org,route,model,reason}` and a daily report of top throttled routes/orgs.

Devon: Agreed. Also recommend we tag logs with `throttle_reason` and `quota_bucket_id` so postmortems can quickly map to policy rows. Example logging enhancement: `logger.info(\"throttle\",{org,route,model,reason,remaining_tokens,reset_ts,quota_bucket_id})`.

Claire: What do we send back to customers in the ticket? I can draft reply: explain that their burst exceeded per-org RPS and token quota, show the evidence (grafana chart screenshots), offer temporary bump and best practices (streaming, lower max_tokens, client-side backoff).

Devon: +1. Include repro steps so they can run a smaller test and avoid production traffic causing more throttles. Also send them the `X-RateLimit-*` header explanation and link to our docs page (internal: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/quotas).

Ram: Follow-up actions (assignments):
- Claire -> Draft customer update and confirm acceptance of 6-hour bump (ETA 30m)
- Ram -> Keep monitoring, roll back bump if not needed earlier (ongoing)
- Kai -> Create a GH issue to add `throttled.by_route` metric and Console panel (PR draft by EOW)
- Devon -> Add a short KB for support with quick triage checklist and queries (done today)

SRE-Oncall-Bot: Incident note: created incident-2026-11-21-acme-throttle for postmortem tracking.

Claire: I'll post the screenshots and the draft to the ticket thread. If customer pushes for root cause, we'll point to traffic pattern (bursting fan-out + large max_tokens) and quota policy.

Devon: One last reproduction tip for engineers: when testing, use streaming (`?stream=true`) and smaller `max_tokens` to mimic production pacing. If reproducing locally, ensure you inject the `X-Org-ID` header to use the same quota bucket. Example header: `X-Org-ID: acme-ml`

Claire: Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open until bump ends and metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
